svg.title: Skipping the months a query can't match
svg.desc: An animation in four steps. A query asks for the matches played in March, from a matches table with one partition per month, January to April 2026. The planner compares the query's played_on range with each partition's bounds and prunes January, February, and April. Only matches_2026_03 is scanned, and its 3 rows are returned while the pruned months stay dark. Then a query for the matches that Koala, player 1042, won filters on winner_id instead. It puts no limit on played_on, so the planner keeps every month, and the scan reads all 12 rows to return 2.
svg.text: Skipping the months a query can't match
The planner compares the WHERE clause with each partition's bounds and scans only the partitions that could hold the rows the query wants.

g.text: partitioned by the month of played_on

svg.text: A query asks for the matches played in March: played_on from 2026-03-01 up to, but not including, 2026-04-01.
The planner compares that range with each partition's bounds. Only March can hold rows in that range, so it prunes the other three months.
Only matches_2026_03 is scanned, and all 3 of its rows are returned. The pruned months stay dark, and none of their rows is read.
A query for the matches Koala (player 1042) won filters on winner_id, not played_on, so no month can be pruned. All 12 rows are read to return 2.
